notes.text: The source gives R. Nasa’s statement on treating the deceased as a met mitzvah.
The exact chapter names R. Ḥanina bar Sisi in a separate story. Heilprin brings this as a name parallel, not as a second witness to the same zimmun narrative.
Nasa recalls repeated meals with R. Taḥlifa Abba and his uncle Aninyaya bar Sisi, who omitted him from the zimmun before puberty. The glossed Sanhedrin name belongs to another episode.
The compared Berakhot witness has Aninyaya bar Sisai. Keep the root’s Ininyah and its accompanying Ḥanina name comparison rather than normalizing them.
The named chain is present: Nasa transmits a proof from R. Elazar about sanctifying the Name.
Both chains appear, from R. Yonah on the place of restitution and from R. Yose ben Ḥanina on the point at which payment is considered made.
The opening halakhah has R. Yonah relate Nasa’s question about carrying between the corner boards.

The father’s rule is reported by Nisa through his mother. The underlying sentence includes a condition for one who has no ordinary oil. Heilprin excerpts the ruling without that condition, which belongs in the contextual note.
R. Redifah transmits Nisa’s question about joining three adjacent areas. The printed name remains Nisa here.
Dinei Mamonot remains provisional. Checked the potential Yerushalmi Sanhedrin chapters and located Nasa transmitting Elazar in Sheviit, but the precise numbered Sanhedrin passage remains open.
The consulted Bava Kamma unit is the flooded-donkeys case and does not contain the named chain. Chapter numbering and another witness remain possible.
